newsitem.title: USA: U.S. tobacco shares slip after high court ruling.
newsitem.headline: U.S. tobacco shares slip after high court ruling.

text.p: Shares in U.S. tobacco companies slipped on Monday after the U.S. Supreme Court rejected a constitutional challenge to a Florida law allowing the state to sue cigarette makers for the cost of smoking-related illnesses.
Tobacco industry analysts said the high court ruling was not a surprise but added to recent investor jitters about cigarette-makers' stocks.
Philip Morris Cos Inc was off 4-1/8 to 125, RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp eased 7/8 to 33 and Loews Corp slipped 2-1/8 to 101-1/2.
Supreme Court justices let stand a Florida Supreme Court ruling that the state has the legal right to sue cigarette makers for Medicaid costs incurred by Florida from tobacco-related illnesses.
The ruling cleared the way for Florida's case to proceed to trial, which is set for August.

Sanford Bernstein analyst Gary Black noted the Supreme Court rarely accepts a case prior to trial. "I don't know why the market cares about it because I don't think anyone expected the U.S. Supreme Court to take it on," he said.

But the U.S. Supreme Court ruling came on the heels of a ruling on Thursday by Mississippi's Supreme Court throwing out challenges by the state's governor and the tobacco industry that would have kept a $940 million case from proceeding to trial in June. That news sent cigarette makers' shares reeling on Thursday.
Monday's ruling "promotes the incentive for the tobacco industry to reach a compromise" with anti-tobacco forces, said Smith Barney analyst Martin Feldman.

The recent setbacks on the litigation front came after tobacco companies had seen some legal rulings break their way. In February a federal judge dismissed a lawsuit brought by the city and county of San Francisco and 11 other California counties against Philip Morris.

Analysts said news on Monday from smokeless tobacco maker UST Inc was company-specific and did not affect other tobacco makers. UST fell 3-7/8 to 29-1/2 after it said it expected a drop in first quarter earnings, mainly because of a decline in its moist smokeless tobacco unit volume.
